name: Moussa Mara
detail: Former Prime Minister and expert-comptable; transparently declares his personal assets and advocates broadening the tax base, ending corporate exemptions, and local tax reform; does not call for an annual net wealth tax.

name: Oumar Mariko
detail: Leader of the SADI party; radical socialist rhetoric against oligarchs and corporate tax exemptions for mining multinationals; does not propose an annual net wealth tax.

name: Gouvernement du Mali (Transition / Assimi Goïta)
detail: Transitional executive fiscal policy focuses on resource sovereignty ("Que l'or brille pour les Maliens"), recovering unpaid taxes and royalties from mining multinationals (Barrick Gold), the 2023 Mining Code, and terminating the France-Mali bilateral tax treaty; no net wealth tax proposed.

name: Coalition Malienne Publiez Ce Que Vous Payez (PCQVP Mali)
detail: Tax justice and transparency coalition; focuses on disclosure of extractive industry contracts, EITI compliance, and tracking community mining funds; does not campaign for net wealth taxation.

name: Coalition des Alternatives Africaines Dette et Développement (CAD-Mali)
detail: Major civil society coalition campaigning against illicit financial flows, debt burdens, and regressive VAT; advocates equitable taxation without calling for a stock-of-wealth tax.

name: Union Nationale des Travailleurs du Mali (UNTM)
detail: Peak trade union confederation; fiscal advocacy focuses on reducing personal income tax on salaries (ITS), fighting high living costs, and corporate tax evasion; no wealth tax motion.

name: Étienne Fakaba Sissoko
detail: Economist, Director of CERA, Associate Professor at University of Bamako; comments on macroeconomic policy, debt, and public finance; does not advocate a net wealth tax.

name: Aminata Dramane Traoré
detail: Author, anti-globalization activist, former minister; critiques structural adjustment and imperialist resource extraction; does not propose wealth taxation.

name: Délégation du Mali à l'ONU (Groupe Africain)
detail: Voted in favour of UN General Assembly Resolution A/RES/78/230 on a UN Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation; focuses on international corporate tax avoidance and inclusive rulemaking without calling for a wealth tax.
